answer: Agents can resist sybils by proving they hold unique storage over time. Each identity must keep a large random dataset and answer surprise challenges about it; a hollow identity sharing one disk with others fails because the answers must arrive faster than data can be fetched. Rewards trickle out like nectar only after weeks of passing audits, so trust grows at a glacier pace. An attacker pays the full disk and bandwidth cost for every fake, with nothing earned until much later.
